data.description:
## The gap

Two DIFFERENT tickets hit the same `sys.path` divergence on 2026-09-04/05, hours apart, in
opposite directions:

- `7f46-790d-7b9f-4db1` — a test module resolved its import only because some earlier-collected
  test had already put `scripts/` on `sys.path`. It passed under `python -m pytest` and failed
  under the BARE `pytest` console script.
- change 2647 (`ff4a-2832`, op-cert binding) — a new test used a `tests.`-rooted import. It passed
  locally under `python -m pytest` and failed in CI under the bare console script, costing a
  **23-minute** gating cell and a full re-push, on a queue that was already saturated.

The rule is real and the guards exist (`tests/unit/test_tests_import_convention.py`,
`tests/unit/test_scripts_import_convention.py`) and they WORK — the second case was caught exactly
as designed. The problem is WHERE it was caught.

## Why it costs a full CI cycle

`python -m pytest` puts the current directory on `sys.path`; the bare `pytest` console script does
not. `make test` and CI use the bare script. So a developer or agent who verifies with
`python -m pytest` — the more common habit, and the form that works for almost everything else —
gets a green that CI will not reproduce, and learns about it 23 minutes later from a `Verified -1`.

The full local contract, `make verify`, DOES catch it, but it costs 20-25 minutes and is documented
as a once-before-push step. The cheap check is a couple of seconds:

    pytest tests/unit/test_tests_import_convention.py tests/unit/test_scripts_import_convention.py

run with the BARE console script. Nothing points anyone at it at the moment they need it.

## Why this is worth fixing rather than filing under "read the docs"

The failure is invisible at the point of the mistake and expensive at the point of discovery, which
is the worst possible ordering. It also selects against the careful: an agent that runs a targeted
subset before pushing (rather than the full 25-minute suite) is exactly the one this catches out.
Two independent instances in a single night is enough evidence that habit is not going to fix it.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The cheap import-convention check is named in the documented pre-push path, with the
      explicit warning that it must be run with the BARE `pytest` console script and that
      `python -m pytest` cannot detect this class at all.
- [ ] The distinction is stated where the mistake is made — a comment or docstring in each
      convention test saying, in one line, why `python -m pytest` shows a false green.
- [ ] A developer following the documented pre-push path catches a `tests.`-rooted import before
      pushing. Proven by deliberately introducing one, running the documented path, and observing
      it fail — not by asserting the docs now mention it.
- [ ] Consider (decide either way, with a reason recorded) whether the guards should ALSO run under
      a fast lint-adjacent target so the check is unavoidable rather than remembered.
data.title: Import-convention violations are invisible under python -m pytest and only surface 23 minutes later as a CI Verified -1: two independent instances in one night
